_comment: Normative statements that an accepted decision has retired, and what replaced them.
scripts/check-retired-guidance.py fails when one appears as a live directive.
A line carrying a retired pattern is allowed when it also carries one of the
entry's `citation_markers` -- naming the superseding decision, or saying the
guidance is stale. That is the difference between DIRECTING against accepted
architecture and RECORDING that the old rule was retired, and only the first
is a defect. It also means the fix is never to delete the history: cite the
Add an entry whenever a decision supersedes normative text that is written
down somewhere else, so the retired phrasing cannot quietly outlive it.

entries.replacement: maistro-core carries the soft scope axes global -> org -> team -> user -> agent -> session; only the hard `tenant` boundary is Stronghold-specific. The retired shorthand conflated scope with tenancy.

entries.pattern: (?i)(nothing is ever executed|only stamps? a timestamp)
entries.replacement: Due schedules admit canonical Runs through the Container-wired ScheduleRunAdmitter, and POST /v1/schedules/{id}/run fires a real Run (409 when it cannot); the durable ScheduleStore cursor advances only after a Run exists. Remaining convergence is #251: run_registered_dag DurableRunStore is disjoint from the canonical RunStore.

learnings.embedding is vector(1536) with an HNSW cosine index (migration 011); memory_entries.embedding was repaired from text to vector(1536) by migration 029. outcomes and episodic_memories deliberately carry no column until a producer writes one. Similarity is schema-ready but not enabled by default: DurableHybridLearningStore needs a caller-supplied embedding client and no production entrypoint constructs one.

Scoped pgvector recall is schema-ready and wired but not live by default: the column, index and hybrid store exist, yet no production entrypoint constructs an embedding client, so the column stays NULL and retrieval is keyword/attribute matching without one.
